samples.summary: `buildRowNode` / `buildCellNode` gained a REQUIRED `depth: number` parameter, but three existing call sites still pass one argument
samples.evidence: New signatures: `function buildCellNode(cell: TableCell, depth: number)` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:417) and `function buildRowNode(row: TableRow, depth: number)` (:425) — neither has a default. Un-updated callers: `insertTableRow` → `const rowNode = buildRowNode(row);` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:2775); `insertTableColumn` → `buildCellNode(cells[r])` (:2818); `updateTableCell` → `const cellNode = buildCellNode(cell);` (:2858). These are TS2554 errors, and packages/frontend has no `tsc` lane at all (vite strips types), so nothing in CI catches them. At runtime `depth` is `undefined`, which falls through to `buildBlockNode(b, undefined)` and re-defaults to 0 — so these row/cell writes restart the nesting count from zero regardless of how deep in the tree they land. Fix belongs on the new code: give `depth` a default or pass the resolved depth at these three sites.

samples.summary: The new nesting cap only guards full-document writes; every incremental block/row/cell write enters `buildBlockNode` at depth 0 and can write past `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`
samples.evidence: `buildBlockNode(block)` (depth 0) is called from paths that write at an ARBITRARY tree depth: `updateBlock` → `tree.editByPath(blockPath, endPath, buildBlockNode(block))` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1723, where `resolveBlockTreePath` resolves paths inside table cells — see `isCellBlockPath` at :1701), `insertBlockAfter` (:2335), the paste path `insertBlocksAfter` (:2371), `insertBlock` (:2312), plus the row/cell writers at :2775/:2818/:2858. So a table block inserted into a cell that is already 30 tables deep is written with its own subtree counted from 0, producing CRDT content deeper than `treeNodeToBlock` will ever materialize (packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:225) — exactly the state `writeFullDocument`'s new refusal says must never exist. The user-facing route is unguarded too: `Doc.insertTableInCell()` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:885) calls `store.insertBlockAfter` with no depth check, and grep finds no nesting check anywhere on the editor's insert-table-in-cell path (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4237).

samples.summary: The backend's twin writer (`writeDocsRoot`) has no nesting cap, and `PUT /content` admits one level deeper than the readers materialize
samples.evidence: `packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:150-200` is the documented mirror of `writeFullDocument` ( see its own comment at :302) but `buildBlockNode`/`buildRowNode`/`buildCellNode` there recurse with no depth parameter and `writeDocsRoot` (:306) has no equivalent of the new `hasTableAtNestingCap` refusal. `PUT /content` reaches it with a caller-supplied body (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:213), and its validator allows `depth > MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH` only (`assertValidBlock`, :443, with `MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH = 32` at :806) — a table at nesting depth 32 passes, while `treeNodeToBlock` truncates any table at `depth >= 32` to `rows: []` (packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:225). verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. The truncating reader is real and shared: docsTreeToDocument/treeNodeToBlock returns `rows: []` for any table at depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH (packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:219-229, table-nesting.ts:26), and the backend's readDocsRoot delegates its whole walk to it (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:239-257). The cited bypassing site exists exactly as described: document-copy.service.ts:428 reads the source with readDocsRoot and :445 hands that same truncated model to writeDocsRoot, which is a documented wipe-and-rewrite (docs-tree.ts:306-327, editByPath removal then editBulkByPath). No equivalent of the new hasTableAtNestingCap guard exists on the backend — grep finds it only in packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:446, and writeDocsRoot/buildBlockNode (docs-tree.ts:150-200, 306-354) apply no depth cap. The only backend depth validator, assertValidBlock with MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH = 32 (api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:438-447, :806), is called only from the v1 PUT handler (:190), never from the copy service, and it rejects only depth > 32 — so a document whose innermost table sits at exactly the reader's cap is accepted and stored, then read back with its rows dropped. A copy of such a document therefore persists the truncation into the new CRDT with no refusal. One nuance that lowers but does not remove impact: the copy target is a freshly created document (document-copy.service.ts:204-232), so no peer's rows are deleted and the source is unharmed — the harm is silent row loss in the copy rather than a replicated deletion. seed-templates.ts:79 does call writeDocsRoot unguarded, though its input is repo-authored seed content rather than a truncated read, making that secondary reference weaker. No refutation ground applies: the code is present, reachable, and unguarded.

The budget lives inside the shared exported helper `expandCellRangeForMerges` (packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:40,114-142), so it applies to every consumer, not just the render path its doc comment (selection.ts:29-38) reasons about. finding.summary: DOCX import recurses into nested tables with no depth cap, and the model it produces then flows into uncapped recursive consumers (text/markdown serializers, DOCX exporter) — the layout cap the diff adds is the only producer-independent bound
finding.evidence: `DocxImporter.convertTable` calls itself for every `<w:tbl>` inside a cell (packages/docs/src/import/docx-importer.ts:415) with no `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` check, so a crafted .docx overflows the stack during import — before any layout runs. If it survives import, the resulting >32-deep `TableData` is walked by uncapped recursions outside the layout: `packages/docs/src/serialize/text.ts:60/76/87` (`blockToText`→`tableToText`→`cellToText`→`blockToText`, used by clipboard `text/plain`) and `packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:202` (`blockToXml`→`tableToXml`→`blockToXml`). `packages/docs/src/view/table-layout.ts:145` explicitly justifies its own cap by "the layout takes documents from other producers too (DOCX import, paste)"; that same argument applies to the importer and to these serializers, which the change leaves unbounded.

verdict.reason: The finding claims DocxImporter.convertTable recurses into nested tables with no MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH check. It does have one: packages/docs/src/import/docx-importer.ts:437 gates the recursive call with `if (depth + 1 < MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH)`, the constant being imported at docx-importer.ts:11 from model/table-nesting.ts:26 (=32). convertTable takes `depth = 0` (docx-importer.ts:261-265) and both top-level entry points (docx-importer.ts:136 body walk, :769 header/footer walk) start at 0, so every nested descent passes the guard. The doc comment at docx-importer.ts:247-259 states precisely the reasoning the reviewer says is missing, including that capping the producer is what bounds the uncapped serializers (serialize/text.ts, serialize/markdown.ts, docx-exporter). The cap is enforced on every other producer too (model/crdt-tree.ts:225, frontend yorkie-doc-store.ts:390/449/523, snapshot-adapters.ts:152), and a regression test at packages/docs/test/import/docx-importer.test.ts:1450-1460 imports MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH+10 nested tables and asserts the result is exactly the cap. The reviewer's cited evidence line 415 is `colIdx += effectiveSpan;` in the vMerge-continue branch, not the recursion. Since no producer can emit a model deeper than the cap, the derivative claim about the text/markdown/docx-export recursions being reachable at >32 depth falls with it.

finding.summary: The truncating reader's output can be written back to the CRDT, making the read-time truncation a permanent deletion of rows below the cap
finding.evidence: `setHeader` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:903-911) and `setFooter` (:942-950) take `this.getDocument()` — the document produced by the now-capped `treeNodeToBlock` (:466-484), where a table at depth ≥ MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH reads as `rows: []` — and, on the treeless fallback path, hand it to `writeFullDocument`, which rebuilds every node via `buildBlockNode` (:3221). `setDocument` (:986-996) has the same shape. The reader's 'degrade, do not vanish' promise only holds for reads; any round-trip through these writers persists the truncation into the shared tree, so the content 'nobody can then open to repair' becomes content nobody can repair at all. Fix belongs on the write path (refuse to rewrite a truncated table, or mark truncated tables so writers skip them).

verdict.reason: The finding says `writeFullDocument` takes the truncated `getDocument()` model and rebuilds every node via `buildBlockNode`, persisting the read-time truncation, and that the fix belongs on the write path. That guard already exists at the head of `writeFullDocument`: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:3260-3271 calls `hasTableAtNestingCap` on `document.blocks`, `document.header.blocks` and `document.footer.blocks` and throws 'refusing to rewrite the document: a table is nested at or past N levels…' before any `buildBlockNode` call (:3272-3295). `hasTableAtNestingCap` (:446-457) uses the same depth convention as the reader's truncation (`treeNodeToBlock` :522-527), so exactly the tables that read as `rows: []` trip it. All three cited entry points route through it: `setHeader` treeless fallback (:952-958, call at :954), `setFooter` treeless fallback (:991-997, call at :993), and `setDocument` (:1029-1039, call at :1039). The behaviour is pinned by tests at packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:3658-3671 ('refuses a full write of a document that reached the cap' expects the throw). The only other `buildBlockNode` write paths — the tree-present branches of `setHeader` (:967) and `setFooter` (:1008) — build from the caller-supplied header/footer argument, and a repo-wide grep finds no callers of `setHeader(`/`setFooter(` in packages/frontend/src besides the definitions, so no truncated round-trip is reachable there either.

finding.summary: Revision-preview snapshot path recurses over the raw tree before `docsTreeToDocument`'s new nesting cap can apply
finding.evidence: `normalizeYsonTreeNode` (packages/frontend/src/components/history/snapshot-adapters.ts:123-143, recursive call at :140) walks the whole parsed snapshot tree with no depth bound and only then hands the result to `docsTreeToDocument` (:178), which is the reader the PR bounded with `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` (packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:225). A `block > row > cell > block > table > …` chain written by a peer — precisely the hazard `model/table-nesting.ts:11` says no attribute band can reach — therefore overflows the stack in this pre-pass and throws a `RangeError` out of `parseDocsSnapshot`, so the version-history preview still crashes on the document the cap was added to keep openable. The cap protects the live store (`packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:480`) and the engine reader but not this consumer; the fix is a depth bound in `normalizeYsonTreeNode`. I could not confirm how deep a tree the server-stored snapshots can actually carry, hence low confidence, but the path is reachable from the preview UI.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts `normalizeYsonTreeNode` recurses over the raw snapshot tree "with no depth bound," citing lines 123-143 with the recursive call at :140. The code is not as described. The function is at snapshot-adapters.ts:134 and its signature is `normalizeYsonTreeNode(node, depth = 0)`; `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` is imported at :4 and applied at :151-157, where `const isRow = node.type === 'row'` gates the recursion with `if (!(isRow && depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH))` and passes `childDepth = isRow ? depth + 1 : depth` into the recursive call at :155. Line :140, cited as the unguarded recursion, is actually `const decoded = JSON.parse(raw)` inside the attribute-decode loop. The unit counted matches the engine reader it feeds: crdt-tree.ts:225-229 caps at `depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` and increments per `row` child via `treeNodeToRow`, and the pre-pass counts the same `row` ancestors, so the exact hazard chain named in the finding (`block > row > cell > block > table > ...`, which contains a `row` at every nesting level) is truncated in the pre-pass at 32 levels, yielding the same table-with-no-rows the capped reader produces. Grep for `normalizeYsonTreeNode` repo-wide returns only snapshot-adapters.ts:134/155/195, so there is no second unbounded copy on the preview path reached from revision-preview.tsx:88. The claimed stack overflow out of `parseDocsSnapshot` therefore cannot occur on the described input. One residual, outside the finding as raised: the bound counts only `row` nodes, so a non-table `block > block > ...` chain would still recurse unbounded — but the engine reader `treeNodeToBlock` does not bound that either, so it is not a bypass this consumer introduces.

finding.summary: Sibling clamp on the model path still spreads row widths (`Math.max(0, ...rows.map(...))`) — the exact RangeError the new normalizeCellRange comment says it folded to avoid
finding.evidence: `normalizeCellRange` (packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts) now folds with `reduce` because "`Math.max(...rows)` throws `RangeError` past ~100k arguments, and the row count is a peer's to choose". The same computation on the model path was not changed: packages/docs/src/model/range-slices.ts:57 does `Math.max(0, ...rows.map((row) => row.cells.length)) - 1`. Row count has no band (`numeric-attrs.ts` caps columns via `MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS = 256` but nothing caps rows), so a peer-written table with >~125k rows makes this throw on every style apply / run visit that routes through `visitCellRectangleSlices` (range-runs.ts:81).

verdict.reason: The finding claims packages/docs/src/model/range-slices.ts:57 performs `Math.max(0, ...rows.map((row) => row.cells.length)) - 1`, leaving the model path exposed to RangeError. That code is not present. Line 57 is part of a comment (lines 56-59) that explains why the spread was deliberately avoided; the actual computation at line 60 is `const widestRow = rows.reduce((m, row) => Math.max(m, row.cells.length), 0);`, a fold with no argument-count exposure. Line 61-64 then uses `Math.min(widestRow - 1, ...)`. A repo-wide grep for `Math.max(...` spreads returns no spread-over-rows in range-slices.ts at all — the only hit in that file is the comment string at line 57, which is most likely what the reviewer pattern-matched on. The peer function it cites, normalizeCellRange at view/selection.ts:187-189, folds identically (`table.rows.reduce((m, r) => Math.max(m, r.cells.length), table.columnWidths.length) - 1`), so the two paths agree rather than diverge. The remaining spreads at selection.ts:194-195 are over fixed two-element arrays. Since visitCellRectangleSlices is the function reached from range-runs.ts, the asserted throw on every style apply / run visit cannot occur via the cited mechanism. Refuted as not-present: the model path was changed in exactly the way the finding asserts it was not.
